label: early original-phase v/m/b/j/a/k right after o/k/u/p/j/r/n/2
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase, at positions 1-5 (peaks at t=2-3; 99.9% of mass in the original phase, none at t=0, at <DEL>, or in the copy phase). The current input is nearly always one of v, m, b, j, a, k (v is strongest, then m; these six tokens hold about 95% of mass), usually on its first occurrence. Whether it fires depends on the preceding context: it is strongly favoured when earlier tokens are o, k, u, p, j, r, n, 2. The largest activations come after an o (e.g. x o o [v], f o o j [v]). On its own the token set has low precision (~13%), and adding a previous-token context raises F1 only to ~0.46, which suggests a graded, distributed dependence on the prefix rather than a crisp rule. Does not fire on digits (except a little on 3), most other letters, the delimiter, or copy-phase steps.
